evidence_against: BTC and ETH spot prices were broadly stable to slightly higher versus the predecessor: BTC close declined 0.0117%, while ETH close increased 0.1675%.
Funding rates and open interest declined for both BTC and ETH, which does not show increasing leverage stress; BTC funding fell 38.4% and ETH funding fell 88.9%.
ETH/BTC increased 0.1356%, contrary to a weakening-ETH-relative-performance signal.
The spot observations have extremely low ranges and volumes relative to the predecessor, limiting confidence in interpreting the short interval as a directional market move.
CFGI data are unavailable, so CFGI-component divergence cannot be evaluated.
BTC dominance, total2, total3, stablecoin dominance, ETF flows, and microcap acceleration are not supplied and cannot be inferred.
evidence_for: Top-100 breadth deteriorated over the measured interval: advancers fell from 57 to 44, decliners rose from 27 to 38, and flat constituents rose from 16 to 18.
BTC mark price declined slightly from 64,990.6 to 64,988.6, while BTC spot close declined from 65,022.88 to 65,015.28.
Breadth deterioration occurred alongside declining derivative open interest: BTC open interest fell 1.04% and ETH open interest fell 0.58%.

The observed breadth deterioration partially matches the sequencing component of the pullback-warning hypotheses, although the leverage and price components are mixed or weakening rather than stressed.
Macro observations were unchanged: 10-year yield 4.69%, 2-year yield 4.25%, broad dollar index 119.7034, and VIX 15.15.

summary: Shadow analysis is degraded because CFGI and several rotation/transmission sensors are missing. Current evidence shows breadth deterioration with modestly weaker BTC, but declining funding and open interest plus improving ETH/BTC reduce confirmation of a leverage-driven pullback. Forecast candidates are unratified research objects only.
